FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Community Helpers & Our Neighborhood flashcards.

Twenty-nine helpers, one card each: the people who keep us healthy, keep us safe, feed us, build our homes and teach us something new every day. Show the card, name the helper, then talk about how your neighborhood works — that is the whole method, and it works.

These cards belong to Class 33 · Community Helpers & Our Neighborhood on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Show the card, name the helper

    Hold the card where your child can see the picture and read the helper’s name aloud. Ask "What do you think this helper does?" — then open the card page together and find out.

  2. 02

    Say the words together

    Every card page has a "Say it together" line — a short script in parent words. Say it naturally, then let your child try. The words on the card become the words of your walks around town.

  3. 03

    Spot the helper for real

    After a card, keep it nearby for the day. The mail carrier, the crossing guard and the shop baker are all out there — spotting a helper in real life turns one card into a memory.

  4. 04

    Thank a helper

    Four-year-olds love small jobs. Drawing a thank-you picture for the fire station, or saying "thank you" to the bus driver, teaches gratitude and cements the whole lesson.
